battle.name: 第一次車臣戰爭
battle.brief: 第一次車臣戰爭於1994年末正式爆發，俄羅斯聯邦軍隊在車臣首府格洛茲尼及周邊山區展開激烈城市巷戰與游擊對抗，動員包括大量T-72主力戰車在內的裝甲單位支援步兵突破城鎮防線，並以火力掩護奪取重要據點，展現該坦克的防護與火力優勢。

kit.name: T-72主力戰車
kit.history: T-72是蘇聯於1970年代研製的主力戰車，具備120毫米滑膛炮與複合裝甲，成為俄軍機械化步兵師的核心突擊力量，至今仍在多國服役。

countries: 1994年的直接交戰方並非兩個獲國際普遍承認的國家。聯邦一方是俄羅斯聯邦；在俄羅斯的制度中，格羅茲尼是車臣共和國首府。另一方是宣布主權並以車臣共和國伊奇克里亞名義運作的杜達耶夫政府及其武裝力量。戰區位於北高加索山脈，格羅茲尼河、鐵路和南北向公路把多支縱隊壓進有限走廊。俄軍可從西部、北部、東部與南部進入，並利用達吉斯坦、印古什、斯塔夫羅波爾及銜接鐵路公路作後方；這些地區不是直接交戰方。聯邦軍在兵力、火炮和空中支援上居優勢，車臣一方則利用境內分散據點、村鎮地形與山地通道抵抗。
countriesEn: The direct belligerents in 1994 were not two broadly internationally recognized states. The federal side was the Russian Federation, within whose system Grozny was the capital of the Chechen Republic. The other side was the Dudayev government, which claimed sovereignty and operated under the name of the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria, together with its armed forces. The theater lay in the North Caucasus mountains, where the Grozny River, railway, and north-south roads compressed several columns into narrow corridors. Russian forces could enter from the west, north, east, and south while using Dagestan, Ingushetia, Stavropol, and connecting rail and road networks as rear areas; those regions were not direct belligerents. The federal force had superior strength in personnel, artillery, and air support, while the Chechen side relied on dispersed positions, village terrain, and mountain routes inside Chechnya.
people: 聯邦一端的政治授權來自總統鮑里斯·葉利欽，國防部長帕維爾·格拉喬夫承擔中央軍事責任，總參謀長阿納托利·克瓦什寧負責參謀與部隊調度，地面作戰則主要集中於羅曼·古利亞耶夫指揮的第7合約軍。前線常見部隊包括第131近衛摩步旅、第42近衛摩步師所屬第81近衛摩步團、第276摩托化步兵團及第50特種部隊旅。車臣一端由杜達耶夫掌握國家政治與戰略授權，這位前蘇聯空軍中將並非每天指揮每一支部隊；實際防務更多由國防部長阿斯蘭·馬什哈多夫及地方指揮官處理。這種差異直接影響戰役：聯邦軍能集中大量火炮與航空兵，卻難以迅速解決分散據點；車臣軍難以維持連續防線，卻能保存小單位並反覆選擇交戰地點。
peopleEn: Political authority for the federal campaign came from President Boris Yeltsin. Defense Minister Pavel Grachev bore central military responsibility, Chief of the General Staff Anatoly Kvashnin directed the staff system and force deployments, and ground operations were concentrated mainly under the 7th Combined Army commanded by Roman Gulyayev. Units commonly seen on the front included the 131st Guards Motor Rifle Brigade, the 81st Guards Motor Rifle Regiment of the 42nd Guards Motor Rifle Division, the 276th Motor Rifle Regiment, and the 50th Special Forces Brigade. On the Chechen side, Dzhokhar Dudayev held national political and strategic authority. This former Soviet Air Force lieutenant general did not personally direct every field unit day by day; practical defense was handled more often by Defense Minister Aslan Maskhadov and local commanders. That difference directly shaped the campaign: the federal force could mass artillery and aviation but struggled to eliminate dispersed positions quickly, while the Chechen force could not maintain a continuous front but could preserve small units and repeatedly choose the places of engagement.
kits: 俄軍裝備以蘇聯解體後仍可運作的標準系統為主，包括T-72B與T-80BV主戰坦克、BMP-2步兵戰鬥車、BTR-70與BTR-80裝甲運兵車及BRDM-2偵察車。火炮包括2S19 Msta-S自走式152公厘榴彈砲、2S3 Akatsiya 122公厘自走砲、BM-21 Grad火箭砲及1989年列裝的TOS-1A 130公厘突防砲；航空支援可由Su-24、Su-25、Mi-24攻擊直升機和Mi-8T運輸直升機提供。步兵裝備包括AK-74步槍、RPG-7、9M14 Ataka反裝甲飛彈，以及7.62×39公厘、5.45×39公厘和12.7公厘弹药。車臣軍則使用庫存與繳獲的AK-47、AK-74、PKM、DShK、SVD、RPG-7，以及少量T-34、T-72、BMP-1和BTR-70。數量最多的障礙不是武器名稱，而是維修、備件、駕駛訓練與不同規格弹药的供應不均。
kitsEn: Russian equipment centered on standard Soviet-era systems that remained operational after the Soviet collapse, including T-72B and T-80BV main battle tanks, BMP-2 infantry fighting vehicles, BTR-70 and BTR-80 armored personnel carriers, and BRDM-2 reconnaissance vehicles. Artillery included the 2S19 Msta-S 152 mm self-propelled howitzer, the 2S3 Akatsiya 122 mm self-propelled gun, the BM-21 Grad rocket artillery, and the TOS-1A 130 mm assault gun fielded in 1989. Air support could be supplied by Su-24 and Su-25 aircraft, Mi-24 attack helicopters, and Mi-8T transport helicopters. Infantry equipment included AK-74 rifles, RPG-7 launchers, 9M14 Ataka anti-tank guided missiles, and 7.62×39 mm, 5.45×39 mm, and 12.7 mm ammunition. Chechen forces used stockpiled and captured AK-47 and AK-74 rifles, PKM and DShK machine guns, SVD rifles, RPG-7 launchers, and small quantities of T-34, T-72, BMP-1, and BTR-70 vehicles. The greatest limitation was not the availability of weapon names but maintenance, spare parts, driver training, and inconsistent ammunition supply.
tactics: 12月11日的炮擊與空襲只是聯邦作戰的第一階段，真正的攻勢由多個地面縱隊展開。第131近衛摩步旅由北面經薩馬什基向阿爾漢卡拉推進；第81近衛摩步團沿塔爾斯科耶、新孫日哈一帶的鐵路與公路向格羅茲尼壓進；第276摩托化步兵團由東面巴亞尤爾特方向切入；南部部隊則沿弗拉季卡夫卡茲、別赫別赫與列丹特之間的道路和鐵路接近市區。縱隊企圖先奪取橋梁、道路交叉口和鐵路節點，再讓後續部隊展開。車臣游擊隊沒有建立完整而連續的正面，而是以反裝甲伏擊、定點遲滯、短時間集中火力及縱深撤退切斷車隊。部分俄軍坦克在前進中距步兵過遠，裝甲車內的步兵未能及時展開，長隊形因此容易在狹窄道路上停滯。進入格羅茲尼後，街道、瓦礫和樓房把縱隊切成短距離戰鬥。聯邦軍逐步改用工兵清理樓房、步兵逐棟推進、坦克在路口提供短距離直射火力，並以炮兵和航空兵支援已知火力點。1995年3月，車臣武裝在薩馬什基至阿爾漢卡拉一線反擊過度延伸的第131旅，迫使聯邦軍再次收縮。此役後，聯邦軍縮短單次推進距離，加強護衛、工兵掩護、故障車輛回收與晝夜交替的補給安排。
tacticsEn: The artillery bombardment and air attacks of December 11 were only the first phase of the federal operation; the real offensive unfolded through several ground columns. The 131st Guards Motor Rifle Brigade advanced from the north through Samashki toward Alkhan-Kala. The 81st Guards Motor Rifle Regiment pushed toward Grozny along the railway and road around Tarskoye and New Sunzha. The 276th Motor Rifle Regiment cut in from the east around Babayurt, while southern units approached along the road and railway corridor through Vladikavkaz, Bekh-Bekh, and Redant. The columns sought to seize bridges, road junctions, and railway nodes before deploying the units behind them. Chechen fighters did not establish a complete continuous front; instead, they used anti-tank ambushes, localized delays, brief concentrations of fire, and withdrawals into depth to cut the columns. Some Russian tanks moved too far ahead of their infantry, while dismounts inside armored vehicles could not deploy promptly, making long formations vulnerable to stalls on narrow roads. After entering Grozny, streets, rubble, and buildings reduced every operation to short-range fighting. Federal forces increasingly used sappers to clear structures, infantry to advance building by building, tanks to provide direct fire at intersections, and artillery and aviation to support identified strongpoints. In March 1995, Chechen fighters counterattacked the overextended 131st Brigade along the Samashki to Alkhan-Kala line and forced federal units to contract again. The federal command subsequently shortened individual advances and strengthened convoy escorts, engineer cover, vehicle recovery, and alternating day-and-night resupply.
data: 關鍵日期構成了一條清楚的戰役時間線。杜達耶夫於1994年10月11日當選車臣總統；12月初，車臣武裝力量在格羅茲尼控制聯邦機構並扣押代表，使莫斯科把局勢判定為國家緊急狀態。俄羅斯國家杜馬在12月7日完成使用武力的授權，葉利欽於12月9日至10日簽署命令，聯邦炮兵與航空兵在12月11日開始攻擊。第81近衛摩步團約在12月17日控制新孫日哈，12月28日前後取得格羅茲尼火車站並逐步控制機場，12月29日至31日先頭部隊進入市中心。總統府在1995年1月4日被聯邦軍攻占，1月6日聯邦旗幟升上市中心廣場，但戰鬥沒有當日結束。1995年3月9日至31日，薩馬什基至阿爾漢卡拉一線爆發第二次薩馬什基戰鬥；4月21日，杜達耶夫在漢卡拉附近的直升機事故後身亡；8月6日，議會選舉馬什哈多夫為總統。城市主要戰術行動延續至1995年盛夏，聯邦軍其後以控制市中心、交通線和大型建築物為主。聯邦軍於1996年1月7日開始分批撤出格羅茲尼，至3月底完成主要撤離；12月12日簽署的哈薩維尤爾特協議則為政治與軍事衝突設定了停火框架。首批聯邦部署常被估為約三萬至四萬人，坦克、步兵戰鬥車與裝甲運兵車合計達數百輛，但各團番轉、封存單位與後續增援使實際數字持續變動。後勤以公路和鐵路為主，炮兵使用122公厘、152公厘、120公厘迫擊砲與TOS-1A榴彈，航空兵補充制導與非制導炸彈。冬季結冰、山路狹窄、受損車輛和游擊隊襲擾使油料、備件、輪胎與回收設備成為補給瓶頸；進入城市後，火車站和市中心補給點更處於直接火力之下。
dataEn: The key dates form a clear operational timeline. Dudayev was elected president of Chechnya on October 11, 1994. In early December, Chechen armed forces took control of federal facilities in Grozny and detained representatives, leading Moscow to classify the situation as a state of emergency. The Russian State Duma completed its authorization for the use of force on December 7, and Yeltsin signed the order on December 9 to 10. Federal artillery and aviation began attacking on December 11. The 81st Guards Motor Rifle Regiment controlled New Sunzha around December 17, seized the Grozny railway station and gradually took control of the airport around December 28, and advanced into the city center from December 29 to 31. The Presidential Palace was stormed by federal troops on January 4, 1995, and the federal flag was raised over the central square on January 6, but the fighting did not end that day. The second Battle of Samashki, along the Samashki to Alkhan-Kala line, ran from March 9 to 31, 1995. Dudayev died following a helicopter accident near Khankala on April 21, and parliament elected Maskhadov president on August 6. Major urban operations continued through the summer of 1995, after which federal control concentrated on the city center, transport lines, and major buildings. Federal troops began withdrawing from Grozny in stages on January 7, 1996, completing the main withdrawal by the end of March. The Khasavyurt Agreement signed on December 12 then established a framework for ending the political and military conflict. The initial federal deployment is commonly estimated at roughly 30,000 to 40,000 personnel and several hundred tanks, infantry fighting vehicles, and armored personnel carriers, but unit rotations, stored formations, and later reinforcements continually changed the actual figure. Logistics depended primarily on roads and railways. Artillery used 122 mm and 152 mm rounds, 120 mm mortar ammunition, and TOS-1A shells, while aviation added guided and unguided bombs. Winter ice, narrow mountain roads, disabled vehicles, and guerrilla interference made fuel, spare parts, tires, and recovery equipment major bottlenecks. Once forces entered the city, the railway station and central depots were also under direct fire.
cause: 戰爭的直接背景是蘇聯解體後留下的主權與權力問題。車臣在1991年11月宣布主權，俄羅斯聯邦則拒絕承認其脫離聯邦地位；此後數年間，格羅茲尼的行政機構、武装組織和安全命令逐漸並存。1994年10月杜達耶夫當選，使車臣政府取得更完整的國內政治授權，並進一步拒絕接受俄羅斯聯邦中央對其軍隊與政府的全面指揮。莫斯科擔心車臣的武裝化與其他北高加索衝突相互連結，會使聯邦權威出現無法逆轉的缺口；車臣政府則把俄軍集結視為推翻現有政府的準備。12月初的格羅茲尼武裝突擊和聯邦機構被扣成為立即導火線。杜馬授權與葉利欽簽署命令後，莫斯科已決定以軍事手段解除武裝、恢復聯邦控制；車臣方面則選擇抵抗而非解散政府與軍隊。最初開火雖由俄羅斯發動，但其前方已累積了數年的憲法衝突、軍事集結和相互不承認。
causeEn: The immediate background was the unresolved question of sovereignty and authority left by the collapse of the Soviet Union. Chechnya declared sovereignty in November 1991, while the Russian Federation refused to recognize its separation from the federation. Over the following years, Grozny developed parallel administrative institutions, armed organizations, and security commands. Dudayev's election in October 1994 gave the Chechen government stronger domestic political legitimacy and further confirmed its rejection of full control by the Russian federal center. Moscow feared that the armed organization of Chechnya, together with links to other conflicts in the North Caucasus, would create an irreversible break in federal authority. The Chechen government regarded the Russian troop buildup as preparation for the removal of its government. The armed seizure of federal facilities and the detention of representatives in Grozny in early December served as the immediate trigger. After the Duma authorization and Yeltsin's order, Moscow had chosen military means to disarm the opposition and restore federal control; the Chechen side chose resistance rather than dissolving its government and armed forces. Although Russia fired the first shots, the invasion came after years of constitutional conflict, military concentration, and mutual nonrecognition.
impact: 戰役首先改變了格羅茲尼的物理與軍事面貌。總統府、政府機關、火車站、工業設施和道路網受到嚴重破壞，原本作為聯邦象徵的首都變成難以維持行政運作的戰場。軍事上，俄軍集中坦克、由裝甲車輸送步兵的做法在鄉村公路和城市街道都受到考驗；炮兵與航空兵能壓制已知陣地，卻難以持續追蹤迅速移動的小單位。聯邦軍後來加強工兵與步兵配合，縮短裝甲縱隊前進距離，並把封鎖、控制交通線和穩定補給放在單純追求市區面積之前。車臣軍在格羅茲尼失去大量固定陣地與重裝備，但分散小單位及其指揮關係仍然延續，杜達耶夫在四多月後身亡，馬什哈多夫則接掌政治與軍事領導。雙方傷亡均十分重大，官方公報、後來研究與不同機構統計相差很大，因此沒有可信的單一精確總數。戰役沒有形成穩定政治和解，反而使聯邦軍在國內承受增加壓力，也讓車臣武裝獲得延續其軍事體系的經驗。
impactEn: The campaign first transformed the physical and military character of Grozny. The Presidential Palace, government offices, railway station, industrial installations, and road network were heavily damaged, turning a capital that had served as a federal symbol into a battlefield where administrative operations were extremely difficult to sustain. Militarily, Russian reliance on concentrated tanks and infantry transported in armored vehicles was tested on both rural roads and urban streets. Artillery and aviation could suppress identified positions but struggled to track small units that moved rapidly. Federal forces consequently strengthened engineer and infantry coordination, shortened armored advances, and placed greater emphasis on blocking routes, controlling transport lines, and stabilizing supply rather than merely occupying additional blocks of the city. Chechen forces lost many fixed positions and much heavy equipment in Grozny, but dispersed units and their command relationships survived. Dudayev died more than four months later, while Maskhadov took over political and military leadership. Both sides suffered substantial losses, but official reports, later studies, and figures from different organizations vary greatly, so there is no reliable single exact total. The campaign did not produce a stable political settlement. Instead, it increased domestic pressure on the federal government to set a withdrawal timetable and allowed the Chechen armed forces to gain the experience needed to preserve their military structure.
result: 聯邦軍在1994年12月底進入格羅茲尼，於1995年1月4日攻占總統府、1月6日控制市中心象徵性地完成奪取首都的目標，但城市並未立即平靜。第131旅在1995年3月薩馬什基的失利顯示，聯邦軍即使取得戰術突破口，也可能因前線過長而失去已占據據點。經過後續清剿與封鎖，聯邦軍在1995年盛夏控制了火車站、機場、政府區和多數主要交通走廊，車臣最高指揮體系則在市中心之外繼續運作。這是一個局部軍事成功而非決定性勝負：俄軍未能摧毀車臣的整個領導與武裝體系，車臣一方也未能以軍事手段迫使聯邦軍永久離開。1996年1月至3月的分批撤退結束了聯邦軍對格羅茲尼的實地占領；同年12月12日簽署的哈薩維尤爾特協議要求俄軍完成撤出並禁止俄羅斯武裝力量留在車臣，卻沒有解決車臣的最終政治地位。主要軍事行動通常以1995年8月大規模攻勢收束為界，政治與軍事上的結束則落在1996年的撤軍和停火安排。戰爭留下的實際狀態，是聯邦法律地位與車臣實地控制同時存在、邊界與權力未獲永久解決的分裂局面。
resultEn: Federal forces entered Grozny at the end of December 1994, captured the Presidential Palace on January 4, 1995, and symbolically completed the objective of taking the capital center when they raised their flag on January 6, but the city did not immediately become secure. The setback suffered by the 131st Brigade at Samashki in March 1995 showed that even when federal forces achieved a tactical breach, they could lose positions already occupied through an overextended front. After subsequent clearing operations and blockades, federal troops controlled the railway station, airport, government district, and most major transport corridors by the summer of 1995, while the Chechen high command continued to operate outside the city center. This represented a limited military success rather than a decisive victory. Russia did not destroy the Chechen command structure and armed forces as a whole, while Chechnya did not force the federal military to leave permanently. The phased withdrawal from January through March 1996 ended federal physical occupation of Grozny. The Khasavyurt Agreement signed on December 12, 1996 required the Russian withdrawal to be completed and prohibited Russian armed forces from remaining in Chechnya, but it did not settle Chechnya's final political status. The main military phase is conventionally dated to the tapering of the large offensive around August 1995, while the political and military termination came through the withdrawal and ceasefire arrangements of 1996. The result was a divided situation in which the federal legal position and Chechen territorial control both persisted, with no permanent settlement of borders or authority.
